Pardo, N. and Moya, J.A. (2013). Prospective scenarios on energy efficiency and CO2 emissions in the European Iron & Steel industry. Energy 54, 113-128. http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.energy.2013.03.015

Locators are printed journal page numbers (PDF page = printed - 112). JRC bottom-up model of EU27 iron and steel (extension of a TNO/Tata Steel model); region EU27, base year 2010. Main file: Table 1 direct energy (carrier not split, net of process gases) and direct CO2 for 16 current process steps plus the works power plant (per MWh; efficiency derived 3.6/12.173 and the printed 32%); Table 6 other operating costs (2010 EUR/t, energy excluded) as opex-total; 9 BATs with absolute SEC and CO2 derived as Table 1 value plus the Table 2 change (formula on each row) and incremental capex from Table 4 (MEUR per reference capacity, converted to EUR/t-per-yr or EUR/kW with the formula); continuous casting capex only; new EAF unit of Sect. 4.4 (1.819 GJ/t, 0.140 t CO2/t, 800 kt/yr); 10 innovative technologies with capex, state of development and expected year, plus ULCOWIN (year only). _measures: Table 2 savings with Table 4 investment for all 12 BATs. _other-values: Table 3 IT changes in energy and CO2 (relative to replaced integrated-route processes, not absolute, so not loaded), Table 5 prices, CO2 T&S cost, CO2 price path, scenario results. Not loaded: Figs 6-15 (scenario trajectories, read from charts). Trap: pdftotext drops the minus sign (it is a \x02 control character) in Tables 1-3; signs were restored from the raw bytes and agree with the companion paper Moya & Pardo 2013 except where noted.

(1) No price year for investment costs (Table 4); 2013 used and flagged. Operating costs and prices are stated for 2010. (2) Table 3 caption says specific consumption of the ITs, but values are changes versus replaced processes (negative = reduction). (3) Differences from the companion Moya & Pardo (2013, J. Clean. Prod. 52) for the same model: EAF CO2 0.240 vs 0.098 t/t; organic coating energy 0.758 vs 0.049 GJ/t; power plant CO2 1.989 vs 2.057 t/MWh; scrap pre-heating CO2 change -0.037 vs 0; oxy-fuel CO2 change -0.009 vs +0.008; CCS CO2 changes +0.183/+0.298 vs 0; pellet plant other cost 4 vs 0 EUR/t; CO2 transport and storage 5 vs 21 EUR/t CO2; growth rates for coal and iron ore swapped (1.64/1.20 vs 1.20/1.64). (4) Power plant current efficiency printed 32% in text vs 29.6% implied by Table 1. (5) "HISARMA" misprint for HIsarna. (6) Text calls the BOF the "blast oxygen furnace".
